PC:
Prepares an appropriate operation room set-up for performing deep sedation:
Places nasal cannula with end-tidal CO2 monitoring capability
Has appropriate size bag and mask, handle and blade, LMA, and endotracheal tube available
Places standard ASA monitors appropriately

Administers deep sedation with assistance:
Chooses the sedative and both the appropriate dose and route for administration
Might titrate the sedation to effect as needed
Initiates management under supervision: provides mask ventilation and suctioning as appropriate
Performs more specific management for the complication: administers anti-epileptic drugs
Secures the airway and stabilizes the patient as needed with supervision
Learner should assess patient, including brief assessment of airway, cardiovascular, pulmonary, and neurologic systems.
Learner should provide oxygen to the patient via mask or nasal cannula, ideally with end tidal CO2 monitoring in place.
Learner will outline a plan for sedation for the retrobulbar block and prepare to administer the sedation.
Learner should choose sedation (may include a variety of agents including propofol, midazolam, fentanyl, alfentanil, etc).
Learner should continue to monitor the patient during the block.
Learner should treat seizure with propofol, midazolam, or alprazolam.
Learner should increase oxygen delivery by application of a face mask.
MK: Verbalizes the need for deep but short lasting sedation for the procedure
Verbalizes the likely diagnosis of intravascular injection as complications of retrobulbar block
Verbalize CNS toxicity as a complication of intravascular injection during retrobulbar block
Explains the management of intravascular injection of local anesthetic after retrobulbar block
Learner should identify convulsions as potential seizure.
Learner should identify retrobulbar block as source of intravascular injection of local anesthetic.
For each complication, describe the pathophysiology. In other words, how would you know this was happening?
For each complication, describe the treatment strategy. In other words, what would you do for the patient if you suspected this complication was happening?
SBP: Verbalizes that the patient is seizing, calls for help
Learner should call for Intralipid infusion from the pharmacy.
Learner should ask the CPR and ACLS be started.
Learner should request crash cart brought into the OR and paddles placed on patient.
ICS: Introduces self to the surgical team at the beginning of procedure
Clearly communicates with the surgeon regarding seizure and the need to administer anti-epileptic drugs
Discusses the patient’s condition, pathophysiology, and treatment options with the surgeon and nursing team
Plays a team leader role in management
Gives clear instructions to other team members in a non-threatening calm manner if assistance is needed (e.g. squeeze the bag once every 6 seconds while I am providing a two hand-mask)
Gives positive feedback to other team members (e.g. good job squeezing that bag)
Learner should administer other comfort measures (vocal reassurance, hand holding, etc).
Learner should inform the surgeons when the patient is appropriately sedated to perform the block.
